data.text: [00:05]So, Emma, who was the person who most influenced you when you were growing up? I mean, like a role model … or something?

[00:13.8]Well … erm, my parents both worked a lot when I was young, erm … especially my dad, and … well, he worked abroad a lot of the time so … I would see him three times a year or something. `[00:27]He used to have a job which took him to different countries all the time – mostly Japan and China – so … I only saw him in the school holidays really. `[00:37.6]I lived with my mum, but I was always really close to my grandmother, too. `[00:43]I got on really well with my mum, but I think the person who most influenced me was my grandmother.
[00:50.8]Mmm … Did you see her a lot?

[00:53]Yes. My mum and my grandmother brought me up really. I mean, she didn’t live with us, but she would look after me a lot when my mum was working. `[01:02]I think I would see her almost every day. `[01:05]Erm … I really looked up to my grandmother. `[01:09]She’s … she was a wonderful person. I mean, she was incredibly kind and generous. And she would always spend time with me. `[01:19]You know …, she always seemed interested in what I had to say.
[01:26]George, who do you think was the most influential person in your life when you were a child?

[01:32.9]Erm … well, I was really into ice skating – particularly ice hockey – when I was young. `[01:40]I loved playing ice hockey … I used to be really good! `[01:45]I picked it up really quickly and … and did it all the time, you know. `[01:50.8]I started playing when I was about five and … well … , went on until … eighteen, or something – when I left school. `[01:59]And my coach was an amazing man called Frank. He was a really good trainer. `[02:06]He …, he taught me so much about the sport and was very good at motivating me and keeping me focused. `[02:15]He was a really inspiring person. `[02:18.8]He was a really good mentor … and role model … in many ways.
[02:24]How often did you see him?

[02:26.6]Well, I would see him all the time! You know, … I used to wear my skates more than my shoes probably! `[02:33.7]I mean … I really played a lot. `[02:36.3]I would play six or seven times a week and he was always there. `[02:43]It wasn’t just the training though. I think I really looked up to him. `[02:49]When you asked him something, he wouldn’t say much, you know, but … what he did say always seemed to be the right thing to say. I remember thinking … I want to be like him!
